translations.text: The word which Habakkuk the prophet saw.
How long, O Lord, shall I cry out, and you do not listen? I call to you when I am oppressed, and you do not save me.
Why have you shown me toils and pains, so that I look upon misery and ungodliness? Before me judgment has been made, and the judge takes a bribe.
Therefore the law is made void, and justice does not go forth at all, for the ungodly man overpowers the righteous. Therefore judgment goes forth perverted.
Look, you despisers, and see; and wonder at marvels, and perish, for I am doing a work in your days which you would not believe if anyone told it to you.
For behold, I will raise up the Chaldeans, a bitter and swift nation, which goes across the breadth of the earth to take possession of dwellings that are not its own.
It is terrible and renowned; its judgment shall come from itself, and its word shall go forth from itself.
And its horses shall leap more than leopards and be swifter than the wolves of Arabia; and its horsemen shall mount and ride out from afar, and they shall fly like eagles eager to eat.
The end shall come upon the ungodly, those who stand against them before their faces, and it shall gather captives like sand.
And it shall make sport among kings, and the mighty shall be its plaything; and it shall mock every stronghold, and heap up earth, and seize it.
Then it shall change its spirit, and pass through, and the power of my God shall be gracious to it.
Are you not, O Lord God, my Holy One from the beginning? And we shall not perish. O Lord, you have appointed it for judgment; and he created me to reprove his instruction.
Your eye is pure, so as not to look upon evil, and you cannot look upon suffering. Why do you look upon the despisers, and keep silent when the ungodly swallows up the righteous, one weaker than he?
And you make men like the fish of the sea, and like creeping things that have no leader.
He has drawn [them] up to destruction with a hook, and dragged him in with a net, and gathered him into his drag-net.
Therefore he will be merry and his heart will rejoice; therefore he will sacrifice to his drag-net and burn incense to his net, for by them he has made his portion fat, and his food choice.
Therefore he will cast his nets, and he does not refrain from continually slaughtering the nations.
I will stand upon my watch and climb up upon a rock, and I will look out to see what [?] he will say to me, and what I shall answer to the one who reproves me.
And the Lord answered me and said to me: Write the vision plainly on a tablet, so that whoever reads it may run after it.
For the vision is for an appointed time, and it shall spring forth completely and not in vain; if it delays, wait for it, for the one who is coming will come and will not tarry.
If you draw back, my soul has no pleasure in him; but the righteous shall live by my faith.

And the arrogant and despising man is insolent; he will accomplish nothing at all, he who has enlarged his soul like Hades, and like death he cannot be satisfied; and he will gather to himself all the nations, and receive to himself all the peoples.

Will not all these take up a parable against him, and a riddle as a tale about him, and say: Woe to him who multiplies for himself what is not his own! How long will he make his collar heavy and strong?
For suddenly those who bite him will rise up, and those who plot evil against you will wake up, and you will become plunder for them.
For you have plundered many nations, so all the peoples left over from you will plunder you too, because of human blood and the ungodliness of the land, and of the city and all who live in it.
O you who greedily seek evil gain for your house, so as to set your nest on high and snatch it from the hand of the wicked!
You have planned shame for your house. You have destroyed many peoples along with it, and your soul has sinned.
Therefore the stone will cry out from the wall, and the worm in the timber will speak it.
Woe to the one who builds a city with blood and sets up a city with falsehood!
Is this not from the Lord Almighty? Many peoples will perish in fire, and many nations will lose heart.
For the earth was filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as water will cover it toward the sea.
O you who give your neighbour foaming, muddy dregs to drink and make him drunk, so that he may look upon their caves!
You are filled with disgrace instead of glory. Drink, you too, and be shaken and tremble. The cup of the Lord's right hand has come around to you, and disgrace has gathered upon your glory.

Therefore the ungodliness of Lebanon will cover you, and the misery of the wild beasts will terrify you, because of human blood, and because of the ungodliness of the land, and of the city and all who live in it.
What good is a carved image, that they have carved it? They made it a molten image, a false phantom, for its maker trusted in his own work when he made dumb idols.
Woe to the one who says to wood, "Wake up, rise up!" and to stone, "Be lifted up!" It is only a phantom, for it is a casting of gold and silver, and there is no breath in it at all.
But the Lord is in his holy temple. Let all the earth fear before his face.
The prayer of Habakkuk.

Lord, I heard the report of you and was afraid, O Lord. I considered your works and was amazed. In the midst of the two living creatures you were revealed. As the years drew near you became known. When the times arrived you appeared. When my soul was troubled, in your wrath you remembered mercy.
God will come from Teman, and the Holy One from the shaded, wooded mountain. Pause. His beauty covered the heavens, and the earth was filled with his praise.
His brightness will be like light, and horns are in his hands, and he established the firm love of his strength.
The word will go before his face, and it will go out into the plains in his footsteps.
He stood, and the earth shook. He looked, and the nations melted. The mountains were shattered by his force. The everlasting hills melted, his everlasting ways.
In return for toil I saw the dwellings of the Ethiopians. The tents of the land of Midian will also tremble.
Are you angry with the rivers, O Lord? Is your wrath against the rivers, or is your onset against the sea? For you mounted your horses, and your cavalry is salvation.
You will bend your bow fully against the tribes, says the Lord. Pause. The earth will be split open by rivers.
The peoples will see you and writhe in anguish, as you scatter the flowing waters. The deep gave forth its voice from the height of its wonders.
The sun was lifted up, and the moon stood still in its order. Your arrows went forth as light, and your weapon was like the brightness of lightning.
By a word you will bring the earth low, and in anger you will strike down the nations.
You went forth as the savior of your people, for the salvation of your anointed ones. You brought death upon the heads of the lawless; they will raise up bonds even to their neck, completely.
You crushed the heads of the mighty in astonishment; they will be shaken by it. They will open their jaws like a poor man who eats in secret.
Your horses will go upon the sea, stirring up many waters.

I kept watch, and my heart trembled at the sound of the prayer of my lips, and trembling entered my bones, and my body trembled within me. You will give me rest in the day of my affliction, when I go up to the people of my sojourning.

For the fig tree will not bring forth its fruit, and no produce of the vine will be found. The olive's yield will fail, and the fields will produce no food. The sheep will lack food, and there are no oxen at the mangers.
But I will rejoice in the Lord, and I will be glad in God my Savior.
The Lord God is my strength, and he will set my feet firmly upon the heights. He led me up to victory by his song.
